findings.claim: The history gives the left pole Augustine (413) and starts the right pole at Darby (1830s), which reproduces the standard polemic that a future earthly kingdom for Israel is a nineteenth-century novelty.
findings.evidence: Chiliasm with a literal earthly reign and a restored Jerusalem is the earliest attested view: Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 80–81 (a thousand years in a rebuilt Jerusalem, held by 'right-minded Christians'); Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5.32–36 (the promise of the land to Abraham fulfilled in the resurrection kingdom); Papias (in Eusebius, HE 3.39). A national restoration of the Jews was Puritan teaching long before Darby: Increase Mather, The Mystery of Israel's Salvation (1669). A dispensational reader who sees 'Augustine ... 1646 Westminster ... 1830s Darby' will screenshot it.
findings.fix: Insert before Augustine: "c. 155–180: Justin Martyr and Irenaeus expect Christ to reign a thousand years on earth from a rebuilt Jerusalem, with the promises to Abraham fulfilled in the land (Dialogue 80–81; Against Heresies 5.32)." Optionally add "1669: Increase Mather, The Mystery of Israel's Salvation, expects a national restoration of the Jews."

findings.claim: The one-people side begins with Augustine (413) and jumps to Westminster (1646), making the ancient consensus look Augustinian-Reformed; the second-century witness that the Church is Israel is absent.
findings.evidence: Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 11 and 135 (c. 155-160): Christians are "the true spiritual Israel" and "the true Israelite race"; this is the reading the Orthodox liturgy assumes.
findings.fix: Insert before the Augustine entry: {"when": "c. 160", "what": "Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho: the church of Jews and Gentiles is 'the true, spiritual Israel'."}
